title: Disclosure of child's precise location data
description: The child's device shares live GPS coordinates at regular intervals, disclosing highly sensitive location information to the backend.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted without additional anonymization or minimization.

title: Linkability of location updates over time
description: Regular transmission of GPS coordinates allows linking successive location points to reconstruct the child's movement trajectory.
assumptions: No pseudonymization or frequent ID rotation applied to the data flow.

title: Unawareness of continuous location tracking
description: The child (or guardian) may not fully understand or consent to the ongoing transmission and processing of precise GPS data.
assumptions: Interface or notices do not clearly inform about real-time tracking implications, especially for minors.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify consent mechanisms; inferred from child data sensitivity.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection rules
description: Processing live location data from a child without verified parental consent or appropriate safeguards may violate regulations such as COPPA or GDPR.
assumptions: No evidence of age verification or consent flow in the provided DFD snippet.

title: Storage of precise location pings enables disclosure
description: Writing every location ping to the history store transfers and persists highly sensitive personal location data, violating data minimality as not all pings may be strictly required.
assumptions: Location pings are personal data; store may be queried later leading to disclosure.

title: Backend stores location without user awareness
description: The process writes location history without mechanisms to inform or obtain ongoing consent from the user about persistent storage of their movements.
assumptions: Users may not expect or be notified of detailed location logging to datastore.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover unawareness for internal writes; based on general LINDDUN U threats.

title: Unnecessary location data disclosure in transit
description: The backend forwards raw location pings to the geofencing engine; this explicit transfer of precise, frequent location data across the process boundary may violate data minimality if only zone-entry/exit events are required rather than the raw pings themselves.
assumptions: Location pings contain personal data; the geofencing check could potentially be performed with less granular data or on-device.
uncertainty_note: Context on exact data fields and whether minimisation is already applied is not provided in the flow description.

title: Backend-initiated disclosure of location pings
